findings.rationale: BootstrapModelExecutor accepts caller-selected ledger_path and failure_latch_path values. AttemptLedger exclusivity and slot-consumption checks apply only to that selected ledger. A caller can construct another executor with a different ledger and latch, replay the same authorization receipt, and receive a fresh copy of all 24 slot IDs. The test covers only one ledger/latch pair. The implementation therefore does not impose a candidate-global 24-call ceiling.
findings.required_action: Bind the authorization receipt to one fixed active ledger and latch, atomically acquire a candidate-global execution capability before any provider call, reject alternative paths, and add a negative test proving that two executor instances cannot consume the same slot or exceed 24 aggregate calls.
findings.title: Caller-selected ledgers permit repeated 24-slot bootstrap budgets

findings.rationale: build_quality_gate validates the AI approval and returns full_test_execution=AUTHORIZED_ONCE, but it never invokes consume_ai_test_access_capability. The atomic fixed-path consumption function is not called by any production full-test gate or runner in the materialized source. Re-running build_quality_gate with unchanged inputs reproduces authorization without recording use, so a one-use protected-test approval is reusable.
findings.required_action: Make the sole full-test execution boundary atomically call consume_ai_test_access_capability before accessing protected tests, bind the consumption receipt to the exact approval and inputs, reject every subsequent invocation, and add an integration test covering two attempted executions.
findings.title: The one-use full-test approval is validated but never consumed

findings.rationale: The closure builder runs pytest and Ruff from the repository root as pytest ... tests and ruff check scripts tests. The only intended DG-10 configuration is nested at evals/dg10/pyproject.toml, and no root pytest or Ruff configuration exists. Pytest and Ruff do not discover a child-directory configuration from those root invocations. Consequently the captures do not apply pytest strict-config/strict-markers or the declared Ruff E,F,I,B,UP,RUF,S selection, despite the report treating the nested configuration as part of the executed closure.
findings.required_action: Invoke pytest with an explicit configuration path and Ruff with an explicit --config path, record those commands and the configuration digest, then regenerate the fresh collection, pytest, Ruff, environment identity, worker-closure report, source inventory, and review bundle.
findings.title: R2 pytest and Ruff captures ignore the frozen DG-10 configuration

findings.rationale: The manifest correctly freezes 216 case IDs, category flags, languages, and the 80/122/24 denominators before any candidate.4 result access. It references candidate.4.5 worker closure fa4c57..., which is absent from current-source and the closed bundle. More importantly, the manifest contains no frozen adapter or attempt-ledger identity, while the scorer only requires worker_environment_sha256, adapter_sha256, and ledger_sha256 to be homogeneous across submitted rows. Caller-selected homogeneous identities can therefore define the execution provenance after result access.
findings.required_action: Issue a successor preregistration that materializes its referenced worker closure and freezes exact worker, adapter, ledger schema/root, and dependency identities before any result access; require every per-case receipt to equal those frozen identities.
findings.title: BFCL execution identities remain caller-selected after case preregistration

findings.rationale: The checkpoint declares six append-only entries and a prefix hash but materializes only current entries at sequences 2, 4, and 6. The referenced var/dg10/stage-ledger-candidate.4.2.jsonl is absent from the bundle. Although each included current row has a valid entry hash and the claim matrix agrees on REVIEW_REQUIRED, the missing rows prevent independent verification of global adjacency, the declared prefix digest, and the complete supersession history. The closed bundle therefore does not establish that one reconciled append-only ledger is the state source.
findings.required_action: Materialize the immutable six-row ledger JSONL in the review bundle, bind its size and SHA-256 in the manifest and checkpoint, and replay every global and per-stage link before regenerating the audit bundle.
findings.title: The stage checkpoint omits the append-only ledger needed for reconciliation
